audit.why: Even lane (49.33% WR, 373 games). Mel wins early before soldier stacking; Azir takes over at first item and outscales in teamfights.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer level chart shows blanket 'Skill' on all 7 rows while content win[] and the packet chart both say Mel 1-6, Azir from first item.
audit.why: Content layer and packet levelChart agree; full layer never got the flip. Whys[5] and [6] on the full layer also describe Mel winning stages the chart hands to Azir.
audit.corrected: phases sides set to Mel (0-4) / Azir (5-6) with whys 5-6 rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no numbers; dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were tradeGood/tradeBad pasted verbatim; Azir E shield-absorbs-burst interaction unstated.
audit.why: Azir E (Shifting Sands) is 22s rank 1 / 16 max, his only dash AND a shield that eats Mel's burst window; Q is 14s rank 1; R Emperor's Divide 120s is his answer to her all-in. Soldier stabs are auto-replacements Rebuttal answers, but Q's soldier sweep and R's wall are not projectiles.

edits.before: Luden's spike: snare-volley chunks half bars and the execute cleans the remainder. Force contacts.
edits.after: His Nashor's/Blackfire spike: stacked soldiers out-range your volley and shove first. Poke, don't duel.

edits.before: Late Mel is a counter-artillery battery: reflect their poke, snare their dive, and execute the chipped.
edits.after: Full-stack Azir out-DPSes you and Emperor's Divide peels your all-in — eat soldier stabs with W, stay back.

edits.before: - Azir Shifting Sands: matchup-defining — His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. It governs your forward steps. - W Rebuttal spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Azir Shifting Sands (E): 22s at rank 1, 16 at max — his only dash AND a shield that eats your burst; force it, then commit. - Conquering Sands (Q) is 14s early — the slide missed, walk up and volley. - Emperor's Divide: 120s, his one answer to your all-in.

edits.before: Q-volley the last-hit, bank the overwhelm stacks, and keep W glowing — the chip is free while his best spells are hostages.
edits.after: His Q is 14s at rank 1 and E 22s — between casts he can only stab with soldiers, so drop Radiant Volley on every last-hit he walks up for.

edits.before: Burning Rebuttal on chip and then eating the full rotation it existed to return — the reflect is the matchup; spend it like a verdict.
edits.after: Conquering Sands' soldier sweep and Emperor's Divide are not projectiles — Rebuttal answers the soldier stabs, never his engage or his wall.

notes: Suspect name 'Land Emperor's Divide' in wants.foe[1] is a FALSE POSITIVE — 'Land' is a verb, the ability name is correct; left alone. Full-layer chart carried blanket 'Skill' while content win[] was already correct (Mel 0-4, Azir 5-6), so side edits go alone per the chart rule — no win[N] no-ops added. Whys 0-4 already describe Mel winning, consistent with the new sides. Azir soldier attacks are projectile-class (blockable/reflectable), so W-eats-soldier-procs claims in content were left standing. Missing interaction (Azir E shield absorbs burst) folded into breakdown.cooldowns.
